grammar.title: は sets the topic; が points to the subject
grammar.explanation: Think of は as “as for…”. It establishes what the sentence is about. が identifies the subject, often the new or focused information. These are starting uses, not interchangeable English translations.
grammar.example: 私は学生です。
grammar.translation: As for me, I am a student.

grammar.title: A small request: をお願いします
grammar.explanation: Put the thing you want before をお願いします. を marks the thing requested; it is pronounced o.
grammar.example: お茶をお願いします。
grammar.translation: Tea, please.

grammar.title: May I? 〜てもいいですか
grammar.explanation: Join a verb’s て-form to もいいですか. 読む becomes 読んで. Learn the useful request as a whole chunk before memorising all verb groups.
grammar.example: 読んでもいいですか。
grammar.translation: May I read it?

grammar.title: Words change with the relationship
grammar.explanation: 友達に: ありがとう. A polite thank-you: ありがとうございます. A more formal thank-you: 誠にありがとうございます. Formality depends on the situation; longer is not automatically better.
grammar.example: ありがとうございます。
grammar.translation: Thank you.

grammar.title: Give each beat its time
grammar.explanation: おばさん (aunt) and おばあさん (grandmother) differ in vowel length. Small っ holds a beat before a consonant. Small ゃゅょ joins the previous sound. In katakana, ー extends the vowel.
grammar.example: がっこう・コーヒー
grammar.translation: school · coffee

grammar.title: Pitch is a pattern, not stress
grammar.explanation: A Tokyo-Japanese starting example: 雨 (rain) falls after the first mora; 飴 (candy) begins low and rises. Regional patterns differ. These illustrations teach a contrast; the app never scores your pitch.
grammar.example: 雨・飴
grammar.translation: rain · candy

grammar.title: に, で and を with ます verbs
grammar.explanation: に marks a point in time (三時に) or where you go (カフェに行きます). で marks where an action happens (家で勉強します). を marks what the action is done to (映画を見ます). Days of the week usually take に; 今日 and 明日 do not.

grammar.title: ませんか: inviting

grammar.title: い adjectives and な adjectives
grammar.explanation: い adjectives end in い: 寒いです, not 寒いだ. Negative: 寒くないです. な adjectives take な before a noun (静かな町) and じゃないです for the negative (静かじゃないです). きれい looks like an い adjective but is a な adjective.

grammar.title: Past adjectives
grammar.explanation: い adjectives: drop い, add かったです (楽しい → 楽しかったです). Never 楽しいでした. な adjectives: でした (静かでした). いい is irregular: よかったです.

grammar.title: Plain forms: how friends talk
grammar.explanation: With friends and family, Japanese switches to the plain form of the verb: 行きます → 行く, 行きません → 行かない, します → する, 来ます → 来る. Nouns and な adjectives take だ (or nothing) instead of です: 暇だよ, 雨だよ. A question is just rising intonation: 行く？ An invitation: 行かない？ (= 行きませんか). Much anime dialogue between friends is plain; use です/ます with people you don't know well.

grammar.title: と思う and ないで

grammar.title: Plain past: た
grammar.explanation: The plain past is the て-form with た instead of て, and だ instead of で: 食べて → 食べた, 行って → 行った, して → した, 寝て → 寝た, 読んで → 読んだ, 飲んで → 飲んだ. Polite equivalents: 食べました, 行きました. い adjectives: おいしかった.

grammar.title: から (because) and もう / まだ
grammar.explanation: Reason + から, result: 疲れたから、寝た ('I was tired, so I slept'). The reason comes first. もう + past = already; まだ = not yet, often answered alone: まだ.
grammar.example: 宿題はもう終わった？
grammar.translation: Have you finished your homework yet?

grammar.title: Abilities and frequency
grammar.formation: Godan: final u-row → e-row + る (話す → 話せる). Ichidan: drop る + られる (食べる → 食べられる). する → できる; 来る → 来られる. Period + に + number + 回.
grammar.explanation: Potential forms state an ability or possibility. Use が for the thing you can do in these examples; を is also used with many potential verbs. The polite negative is ～えません / ～られません. 一週間に三回 gives frequency, while 三時間 gives duration. Colloquial 食べれる exists, but learn 食べられる as the standard form first.

grammar.title: Reasons and first impressions
grammar.formation: Plain predicate + し (noun / な-adjective + だし; polite forms + し also work). い-adjective: drop い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう. いい → よさそう; ない → なさそう.
grammar.explanation: し lists reasons and often leaves room for others: 近いし、時給もいいです. Stem + そう describes a visible impression rather than certain knowledge. おいしそう means it looks tasty, without claiming you have tasted it. Do not confuse this with plain-form + そうです for reported information, introduced later.

grammar.title: Try it; explain the relevant case

grammar.explanation: ～てみる is trying an action to see what it is like, not merely making an unsuccessful attempt. なら takes up a case already mentioned: 週末なら働けます means weekends work for me. It does not promise that the action happens automatically whenever the condition occurs.

grammar.title: Follow the giver and receiver
grammar.formation: Giver は/が + receiver に + thing を + あげる. Giver は/が + me/my side に + thing を + くれる. Receiver は/が + giver に/から + thing を + もらう.
grammar.explanation: The verb chooses the viewpoint. 私はハナさんに本をあげました puts me as giver. ハナさんは私に本をくれました describes a gift coming towards me. 私はハナさんから本をもらいました makes me the receiver. くれる can also refer to a gift to someone on my side; the viewpoint must be clear. Use ordinary forms with friends, not to describe respectful giving to a superior.
grammar.example: レンさんから本をもらいました。
grammar.translation: I received a book from Ren.

grammar.title: Wanting, guessing and suggesting
grammar.formation: Thing が + 欲しい. Plain form + かもしれません (noun / な-adjective: omit だ). Verb た-form + らどうですか.
grammar.explanation: 欲しい expresses the speaker's wish for a thing. Ask another person's wish rather than asserting it without evidence. かもしれません marks uncertainty: 花が好きかもしれません means they may like flowers. 送ったらどうですか suggests sending something; it is not a statement that the sending already happened. Suggestions can sound intrusive, so use them in an appropriate relationship.

grammar.title: Only this much; as much as that
grammar.formation: Number + しか + negative predicate (千円しかありません). Number + も + predicate (一万円もします).
grammar.explanation: しか frames the amount as limited and requires a negative predicate, even though the English sentence is positive: I have only 1,000 yen. Number + も can emphasise an unexpectedly large amount: it costs as much as 10,000 yen. Ordinary number + あります states an amount without either evaluation.

grammar.title: Let's decide; here's my intention
grammar.formation: Godan: final u-row → o-row + う (泳ぐ → 泳ごう). Ichidan: drop る + よう (決める → 決めよう). する → しよう; 来る → 来よう (こよう). Volitional + と思っています.
grammar.explanation: The volitional proposes a joint action or expresses a decision: 行こう, let's go. Use ～ましょう in polite invitations. Volitional + と思っています reports an intention already being held, rather than a settled timetable or an ability. Subject and context determine whether a volitional means 'let's' or 'I'll'.

grammar.title: Prepare something for later
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + おく (買う → 買っておく; 調べる → 調べておく). Polite: ～ておきます.
grammar.explanation: ～ておく links an action to a later purpose. 切符を買っておきます means buying tickets in advance for the trip. It can also mean leaving something in its present state; here we practise the advance-preparation meaning. It does not itself mean an action has already finished; tense and context supply that.

grammar.translation: I'll buy the tickets in advance.

grammar.mistake: Use 調べておく, not 調べるおく. 予約しています can describe an existing reservation; 予約しておきます highlights preparing for later.

grammar.title: A clause can describe a noun
grammar.formation: Plain clause + noun (泊まる旅館; 予約した旅館). No の between a verb clause and the noun. Subjects inside the clause usually take が.
grammar.explanation: Put the description before the noun: 私たちが泊まる旅館, the inn where we will stay; 昨日買った地図, the map bought yesterday. There is no Japanese word corresponding to English 'that' or 'which' in this construction. The tense belongs to the description and its context. Keep the main sentence separate: [泊まる旅館] は駅の近くです.

grammar.title: Who did the favour?
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + あげる / くれる / もらう. Helper に + てもらう; helper が + てくれる.
grammar.explanation: Extend gift viewpoints to actions. ユイさんが手伝ってくれました describes Yui helping me or my side. ユイさんに手伝ってもらいました describes my receiving that help. 私が手伝ってあげました describes my helping someone else. A listener may hear ～てあげる as stressing your favour; avoid offering a superior a favour that way.

grammar.title: Ask gently; apologise specifically

grammar.explanation: ～ていただけませんか is a considerate request for someone to do an action for you. It is a request, not a claim that the action happened. ～てすみませんでした connects a completed mistake to an apology. Name the actual mistake; 遅れて apologises for lateness, not for being busy.

grammar.title: When it happens; what you hope

grammar.title: A report has a source
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + そうです; noun/な-adjective + だそうです. Casual quotation: quoted clause + って.
grammar.explanation: Plain-form + そうです reports information heard or read. 明日は雨だそうです is a forecast report, not your visual judgement. Casual って can quote what somebody said; preserve their content and name the source where it matters. This differs from the adjective stem + そう taught in unit 1: おいしそう describes how food looks, while おいしいそう reports that someone said it is tasty.
grammar.example: 明日は雨だそうです。
grammar.translation: I hear it will rain tomorrow.

examples.ja: レンさんの{話|はなし}では、{出発|しゅっぱつ}は{九時|くじ}だそうです。
examples.en: According to Ren, departure is at nine.

examples.ja: ケンタさんが、{明日|あした}は{晴|は}れるって。
examples.en: Kenta said it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: {新聞|しんぶん}によると、{旅行|りょこう}は{中止|ちゅうし}だそうです。
examples.en: According to the newspaper, the trip is cancelled.

grammar.mistake: A noun needs だ before hearsay そうです: 雨だそうです. 晴れそうです is a visible/likely impression; 晴れるそうです is a report.

grammar.title: Conditions and inferred impressions
grammar.formation: Past plain + ら (晴れたら; 雨だったら). Plain verb/い-adjective or noun/な-adjective stem + みたいです. Negative ない: drop い + くてもいいです.
grammar.explanation: ～たら sets a condition or an event after which something happens; the た is not by itself a claim about the past. Use the context to distinguish 'if' and 'when/after'. ～みたいです expresses an inference or resemblance, rather than reporting a named source. ～なくてもいい permits not doing an action; it does not forbid doing it.
grammar.example: 雨だったら、行かなくてもいいです。
grammar.translation: If it rains, you don't have to go.

examples.ja: {晴|は}れたら、{海|うみ}に{行|い}きます。
examples.en: If it's sunny, I'll go to the sea.

examples.ja: レンさんは{忙|いそが}しいみたいです。
examples.en: Ren seems to be busy.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{教科書|きょうかしょ}を{持|も}ってこなくてもいいです。
examples.en: You don't need to bring the textbook tomorrow.

grammar.mistake: 行かなくてもいい means 'you needn't go', not 'you must not go'. With a noun, say 雨みたいです, not 雨だみたいです.

grammar.title: Before this; after that
grammar.formation: Dictionary-form verb + 前に; noun + の前に. Verb て-form + から.
grammar.explanation: 前に identifies an action before another begins; use the dictionary form even in a past account. ～てから makes the first action precede the second. This is temporal から, not the reason から taught earlier. State the order when a reservation or document depends on an earlier confirmation.

grammar.mistake: Use 出発する前に, not 出発した前に. In AてからB, A comes first; the main verb supplies the overall tense.

exercises.explain: 雨だったら延期するって reports a condition, not an already confirmed postponement.

exercises.prompt: What should happen before buying tickets?
exercises.explain: レンに確認してから、切符を買おう puts confirmation first.

exercises.prompt: Is the teacher's busyness quoted as a confirmed statement by the teacher?
options: No; Kenta infers it from staying late
Yes; the teacher said those exact words
Yes; it is the main class notice
exercises.explain: 忙しいみたい and the following observation make this Kenta's inference.

exercises.context: Report what a forecast said, rather than describing the sky's appearance.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}＿＿です。
exercises.explain: Noun + だそうです expresses hearsay: 雨だそうです.

exercises.context: Say there is no obligation to bring the documents today.
exercises.line: {今日|きょう}は{書類|しょるい}を{持|も}って＿＿いいです。
exercises.explain: 持ってこなくてもいい permits not bringing them. 持ってきてはいけない would prohibit bringing them.

exercises.context: You plan to prepare the documents first, then contact the teacher.
exercises.line: {書類|しょるい}を{準備|じゅんび}して＿＿、{先生|せんせい}に{連絡|れんらく}する{予定|よてい}です。
exercises.explain: てから makes preparation precede contacting the teacher. 連絡する予定 states your plan.

exercises.line: {明日|あした}、{海|うみ}に{行|い}きますか。
exercises.context: You will go only if it is sunny. State that condition.
exercises.explain: 晴れたら gives the required sunny-weather condition.

exercises.line: もう{旅館|りょかん}を{予約|よやく}しましたか。
exercises.context: Not yet: you need to check the date and time first. Choose the reply that says this.
options: はい。もう{予約|よやく}しました。
{予約|よやく}しなくてもいいです。
まだです。{日時|にちじ}を{確認|かくにん}してから{予約|よやく}します。
exercises.explain: Only the first reply states both not yet and checking before booking.

exercises.meaning: I'll check the map before leaving (plain style).
exercises.explain: Dictionary form + 前に marks the later departure; checking the map happens first. The main verb is plain style here.

exercises.context: Looking at Ren working without a break, infer that he is busy.
exercises.line: レンさんは{忙|いそが}しい＿＿です。
exercises.explain: 忙しいみたいです states an inference. An い-adjective does not take だ before hearsay そう.

exercises.prompt: Is the departure time already known in this conversation?
options: No; Kenta says he doesn't know yet
Yes; Ren says it is midnight
exercises.explain: まだわからない answers the question about departure time. Do not borrow the earlier unit's bus time as a new confirmation.

exercises.prompt: Where will Thursday's class take place?
exercises.explain: The notice changes the room from 201 to 302, on the third floor.

exercises.prompt: Does the notice change the class time?
options: Yes; it moves to the afternoon
exercises.explain: 授業の時間は変わりません explicitly keeps the time.

exercises.prompt: Which item is requested, even though textbooks are optional?
exercises.explain: 面接の書類を持ってきてください asks for documents. Textbooks need not be brought.

exercises.prompt: When should students ask their questions?
exercises.explain: 質問は授業が終わってからお願いします puts questions after class.

急いで大学に行きます。
落とし物のお知らせです。

lessons.title: Oops
lessons.description: Describe something's state, say what happened to it, report a lost item and express regret.
lessons.canDo: Identify a lost item's collection conditions and distinguish a change from someone's action

grammar.title: An action and its resulting state
grammar.formation: Person は thing を + transitive verb; thing が + intransitive verb. Intransitive change verb + ている often describes the resulting state.
grammar.explanation: 私は窓を開けました names someone's opening action; 窓が開きました describes the window opening without naming a doer. 窓が開いています describes its open state. Learn each pair as vocabulary; there is no single ending rule that creates every pair. Intransitive 壊れています does not by itself say who broke it.
grammar.example: 窓が開いています。
grammar.translation: The window is open.

examples.ja: ドアを{閉|し}めました。
examples.en: I closed the door.

examples.ja: ドアが{閉|し}まっています。
examples.en: The door is closed.

examples.ja: {電気|でんき}が{消|き}えています。
examples.en: The light is off.

grammar.mistake: Opening something is 窓を開ける; something opening is 窓が開く. Do not replace every を with が while keeping the same verb.

grammar.title: It happened; I regret it
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + しまう. Casual contraction: ～てしまう → ～ちゃう; ～でしまう → ～じゃう.
grammar.explanation: ～てしまう can mark completion or an unwanted outcome. The surrounding action and situation determine whether regret is present. 宿題を全部やってしまいました can mean finishing all the homework; 鍵を落としてしまいました usually conveys regret about losing a key. Recognise contractions in casual speech without using them in a formal apology.
grammar.example: 鍵を落としてしまいました。
grammar.translation: I dropped/lost my key, unfortunately.

examples.ja: {書類|しょるい}を{忘|わす}れちゃった。
examples.en: I forgot the documents (casual, regretted).

examples.ja: {地図|ちず}を{読|よ}んじゃった。
examples.en: I went ahead and read the map (casual completion).

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}を{全部|ぜんぶ}してしまいました。
examples.en: I finished all the preparations.

grammar.mistake: 読んでしまう contracts to 読んじゃう, not 読んちゃう. The form alone does not tell you whether the speaker feels regret.

grammar.title: Usual results, simultaneous actions and regret
grammar.formation: Dictionary/ない form + と + usual result. Verb ます-stem + ながら. Verb ば-form + よかったです (godan: u-row → e-row + ば; ichidan: drop る + れば; する → すれば; 来る → 来れば).
grammar.explanation: ～と presents a regular or automatic result, as in pressing a switch and the light coming on. ～ながら connects two actions by the same subject; the final verb is the main action. ～ばよかったです looks back at an action you wish you had taken. Here ば is taught in this regret pattern; its broader conditional uses come in unit 10.
grammar.example: 出発する前に、確認すればよかったです。
grammar.translation: I should have checked before leaving.

examples.ja: このボタンを{押|お}すと、{電気|でんき}がつきます。
examples.en: When you press this button, the light comes on.

examples.ja: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}きながら、{準備|じゅんび}します。
examples.en: I prepare while listening to music.

examples.ja: {早|はや}めに{予約|よやく}すればよかったです。
examples.en: I should have booked in good time.

grammar.mistake: Use 確認すれば, not 確認するば. Both ながら actions have the same doer. Automatic と is not the pattern for a one-off polite request in the result clause.

dialogues.title: A light and a closed door
dialogues.scene: At the café, Ren checks a light and a door. The lamp is off, not broken; the door is closed. You admit forgetting your documents.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {電気|でんき}が{消|き}えていますね。{壊|こわ}れていますか。
lines.romaji: Denki ga kiete imasu ne. Kowarete imasu ka.
lines.meaning: The light is off. Is it broken?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: いいえ。このボタンを{押|お}すと、つきますよ。
lines.romaji: Iie. Kono botan o osu to, tsukimasu yo.
lines.meaning: No. When you press this button, it comes on.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: あ、つきました。ドアも{閉|し}まっていますね。
lines.romaji: A, tsukimashita. Doa mo shimatte imasu ne.
lines.meaning: Oh, it came on. The door is closed too.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: はい。{雨|あめ}なので、{私|わたし}が{閉|し}めました。お{知|し}らせもドアにあります。
lines.romaji: Hai. Ame na node, watashi ga shimemashita. Oshirase mo doa ni arimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. I closed it because it is raining. The notice is on the door too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {書類|しょるい}を{忘|わす}れちゃった。{準備|じゅんび}しました。でも、{家|いえ}にあります。
lines.romaji: Shorui o wasurechatta. Junbi shimashita. Demo, ie ni arimasu.
lines.meaning: I forgot the documents. I prepared them, but they're at home.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {今|いま}から{持|も}ってこなくてもいいです。{明日|あした}{持|も}ってきてください。
lines.romaji: Ima kara motte konakute mo ii desu. Ashita motte kite kudasai.
lines.meaning: You don't need to bring them now. Please bring them tomorrow.

dialogues.title: Finding out what happened to the key
dialogues.scene: You misplaced your room key before a trip. Kenta helps you read a found-key notice; the dialogue does not claim that this is certainly your key.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {鍵|かぎ}を{落|お}としてしまいました。{急|いそ}いでいたので、よく{確認|かくにん}しませんでした。
lines.romaji: Kagi o otoshite shimaimashita. Isoide ita node, yoku kakunin shimasen deshita.
lines.meaning: I lost my key. I was in a hurry and didn't check carefully.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {出発|しゅっぱつ}する{前|まえ}に、かばんを{見|み}た？
lines.romaji: Shuppatsu suru mae ni, kaban o mita?
lines.meaning: Did you look in your bag before leaving?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: いいえ。{書類|しょるい}を{探|さが}しながら、{準備|じゅんび}していました。
lines.romaji: Iie. Shorui o sagashinagara, junbi shite imashita.
lines.meaning: No. I was getting ready while looking for the documents.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: カフェのドアに、{落|お}とし{物|もの}のお{知|し}らせがあるよ。{鍵|かぎ}が{見|み}つかったそうだよ。
lines.romaji: Kafe no doa ni, otoshimono no oshirase ga aru yo. Kagi ga mitsukatta sō da yo.
lines.meaning: There's a lost-property notice on the café door. It says a key was found.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {私|わたし}の{鍵|かぎ}かもしれません。{出発|しゅっぱつ}する{前|まえ}に、{確認|かくにん}すればよかったです。
lines.romaji: Watashi no kagi kamoshiremasen. Shuppatsu suru mae ni, kakunin sureba yokatta desu.
lines.meaning: It might be my key. I should have checked before leaving.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {交番|こうばん}で{確認|かくにん}しよう。{書類|しょるい}も{持|も}っていこう。
lines.romaji: Kōban de kakunin shiyō. Shorui mo motte ikō.
lines.meaning: Let's check at the police box. Let's take the documents too.

readings.title: A key has been found
paragraphs: {落|お}とし{物|もの}のお{知|し}らせです。
{昨日|きのう}の{午後|ごご}{四時|よじ}ごろ、カフェの{前|まえ}で{鍵|かぎ}が{見|み}つかりました。
{青|あお}い{小|ちい}さなかばんの{形|かたち}のキーホルダーがついています。
{鍵|かぎ}は{駅|えき}の{交番|こうばん}に{届|とど}けました。
{受|う}け{取|と}る{時|とき}、{名前|なまえ}がわかる{書類|しょるい}を{持|も}ってきてください。
カフェでは{受|う}け{取|と}れません。
{出発|しゅっぱつ}する{前|まえ}に、{交番|こうばん}の{場所|ばしょ}を{確認|かくにん}してください。

glosses.kana: かくにんしてください

watch.prompt: Optionally find up to five lines in your own show about a state, an unwanted event or regret. Note whether the line actually names a doer. A state alone is not evidence about who caused it.

exercises.prompt: Is the café light broken?
options: No; pressing the button turns it on
Yes; Ren cannot turn it on
exercises.explain: Ren says no, and You confirms it comes on.

exercises.prompt: Who says they closed the door, and why?
options: You, because the light is broken
exercises.explain: Ren says 雨なので、私が閉めました; 私 belongs to Ren's turn.

exercises.prompt: When does Ren ask you to bring the documents?
exercises.explain: 明日持ってきてください follows permission not to bring them now.

exercises.prompt: Why didn't you check carefully before leaving?
options: Kenta had already found your key
exercises.explain: 急いでいたので gives the stated reason. The found key is not confirmed as yours.

exercises.context: Describe the door's closed state, without saying who closed it.
exercises.line: ドアが＿＿います。
exercises.explain: Intransitive 閉まっている describes a closed state.

exercises.context: Say that you opened the window, naming your action.
exercises.line: {私|わたし}が{窓|まど}を＿＿。
exercises.explain: Transitive 開ける takes the window as its を-marked object.

exercises.context: Looking back, say you should have checked the schedule.
exercises.line: {予定|よてい}を{確認|かくにん}＿＿よかったです。
exercises.explain: する forms すれば in the ばよかった regret pattern.

exercises.line: {書類|しょるい}は{持|も}ってきましたか。
exercises.context: You forgot them. Admit it politely, with regret.
options: はい、{持|も}ってきました。
{忘|わす}れてしまいました。すみません。
{書類|しょるい}を{見|み}つけました。
exercises.explain: 忘れてしまいました admits the unwanted forgetting; the other options say different things.

exercises.line: この{鍵|かぎ}はあなたのですか。
exercises.context: You are unsure and need to check. Do not claim certainty.
options: はい、{絶対|ぜったい}に{私|わたし}のです。
そうかもしれません。{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: かもしれません keeps the identification uncertain and promises to check.

exercises.meaning: I'll prepare while listening to music.
exercises.explain: 聞き is the ます-stem; preparing is the main action, and the same person does both.

exercises.context: Describe the regular result of pressing the switch.
exercises.line: このボタンを{押|お}す＿＿、{電気|でんき}がつきます。
exercises.explain: Dictionary form + と introduces this automatic result. ながら requires a ます-stem and the same doer.

exercises.prompt: Which casual contraction replaces 読んでしまった in this sentence?
exercises.line: {文章|ぶんしょう}を{読|よ}んでしまった。
exercises.explain: でしまった contracts to じゃった; voiced で is retained as じゃ.

exercises.prompt: Where should the owner collect the key?
options: The police box at the station
exercises.explain: The key was handed to the station police box; it cannot be collected at the café.

exercises.prompt: When was the key found?
options: Yesterday around four in the afternoon
exercises.explain: 昨日の午後四時ごろ gives the approximate finding time.

exercises.prompt: Which description matches the keychain?
exercises.explain: 青い小さなかばんの形 describes the keychain; it is not a claim that a bag itself was found.

exercises.prompt: What should the owner bring when collecting it?
exercises.explain: 名前がわかる書類を持ってきてください gives the collection requirement.

lessons.title: Dinner at the Yamamotos'
lessons.description: Visit an older host, recognise respectful language, thank people appropriately and separate expectation from confirmation.
lessons.canDo: Choose wording appropriate to a host and identify the arrangements in a thank-you message

grammar.title: Respect the person doing the action
grammar.formation: 行く/来る/いる → いらっしゃる; 食べる/飲む → 召し上がる; 言う → おっしゃる; 見る → ご覧になる; する → なさる; くれる → くださる. Special polite stems: いらっしゃいます・おっしゃいます・なさいます・くださいます.
grammar.explanation: Honorific verbs raise the person whose action you describe; they do not raise yourself. Use 先生はいらっしゃいます for the teacher's presence, and 私はいます for your own. Honorific vocabulary and です/ます politeness are different: one concerns the actor, the other the listener. Everyday polite verbs remain acceptable in many situations; use the precise honorific target when the task explicitly asks for it.
grammar.example: 先生は何とおっしゃいましたか。
grammar.translation: What did the teacher say?

examples.ja: お{茶|ちゃ}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりますか。
examples.en: Would you like some tea? (respectful)

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{写真|しゃしん}をご{覧|らん}になりました。
examples.en: The teacher looked at the photographs.

examples.ja: {山本|やまもと}さんはいらっしゃいますか。
examples.en: Is Yamamoto-san here? (respectful)

grammar.mistake: Do not describe yourself with 私はいらっしゃいます. いらっしゃいます has the special い stem, not いらっしゃります.

grammar.title: A respectful action or request
grammar.formation: お + native verb ます-stem + になる (読む → お読みになる). Respectful request: お + stem + ください. Some actions use a special verb instead.
grammar.explanation: お読みになる describes a respected person's reading. お読みください requests that action respectfully. Do not stack both constructions or apply お～になる blindly to する compounds. This unit practises common native-verb patterns; compound-specific ご～ forms will receive their own examples later.
grammar.example: こちらをお読みください。
grammar.translation: Please read this (respectful request).

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}はお{帰|かえ}りになりました。
examples.en: The teacher has gone home.

examples.ja: こちらでお{待|ま}ちください。
examples.en: Please wait here (respectful).

examples.ja: このお{知|し}らせをお{読|よ}みになりますか。
examples.en: Will you read this notice? (respectful)

grammar.mistake: Use お読みになります, not お読むになります. お読みください is a request, not a statement that the action happened.

grammar.title: Thank someone; evaluate an outcome; explain an expectation
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + くれてありがとう (close relationship); ～てくださってありがとうございます (respectful). Verb て-form + よかったです. Plain verb/い-adjective + はず; noun + のはず; な-adjective + なはず.
grammar.explanation: Thank a friend with 手伝ってくれてありがとう; thank an older host respectfully with 迎えてくださってありがとうございます. ～てよかった evaluates an action or outcome positively after the fact. ～はず expresses an expectation based on grounds, not certainty and not the obligation of 'should do'. Say what supports the expectation and check it when necessary.
grammar.example: 来てよかったです。
grammar.translation: I'm glad I came.

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}を{手伝|てつだ}ってくれてありがとう。
examples.en: Thank you for helping me prepare (to a friend).

examples.ja: {迎|むか}えてくださって、ありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for meeting me on arrival (respectful).

examples.ja: {六時|ろくじ}に{戻|もど}るはずですが、まだ{確認|かくにん}していません。
examples.en: I expect them back at six, but I haven't checked yet.

grammar.mistake: 戻るはず is an expectation; 戻った says it happened. Advice to return is not 戻るはず. Use ご主人 for someone else's husband, not as a requirement to describe every family's structure.

dialogues.title: An invitation to dinner
dialogues.scene: You and Hana visit Yamamoto-san, an older host. You ask about her husband's expected return; the arrival is not yet confirmed.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {迎|むか}えてくださって、ありがとうございます。{失礼|しつれい}します。
lines.romaji: Mukaete kudasatte, arigatō gozaimasu. Shitsurei shimasu.
lines.meaning: Thank you for meeting us. Excuse me as I come in.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: よくいらっしゃいました。どうぞ、お{入|はい}りください。
lines.romaji: Yoku irasshaimashita. Dōzo, ohairi kudasai.
lines.meaning: Welcome. Please come in.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ご{主人|しゅじん}はいらっしゃいますか。
lines.romaji: Goshujin wa irasshaimasu ka.
lines.meaning: Is your husband here? (respectful)

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {六時|ろくじ}に{戻|もど}るはずですが、まだ{確認|かくにん}していません。
lines.romaji: Rokuji ni modoru hazu desu ga, mada kakunin shite imasen.
lines.meaning: I expect him back at six, but I haven't checked yet.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {鍵|かぎ}は{見|み}つかりました。{交番|こうばん}で{受|う}け{取|と}ってから{来|き}ました。
lines.romaji: Kagi wa mitsukarimashita. Kōban de uketotte kara kimashita.
lines.meaning: The key was found. We came after collecting it at the police box.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: それはよかったですね。お{茶|ちゃ}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりますか。
lines.romaji: Sore wa yokatta desu ne. Ocha o meshiagarimasu ka.
lines.meaning: That's good to hear. Would you like some tea?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい、ありがとうございます。{後|あと}で{大学|だいがく}のことで{質問|しつもん}してもいいですか。
lines.romaji: Hai, arigatō gozaimasu. Ato de daigaku no koto de shitsumon shite mo ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: Yes, thank you. May I ask about university later?

dialogues.title: After the meal
dialogues.scene: You thank the host after dinner. Hana is a close friend who helped prepare the visit, so she receives a different level of thanks.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {夕食|ゆうしょく}、とてもおいしかったです。ごちそうさまでした。
lines.romaji: Yūshoku, totemo oishikatta desu. Gochisōsama deshita.
lines.meaning: Dinner was delicious. Thank you for the meal.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {来|き}てくださって、ありがとうございます。お{土産|みやげ}も、うれしいです。
lines.romaji: Kite kudasatte, arigatō gozaimasu. Omiyage mo, ureshii desu.
lines.meaning: Thank you for coming. I'm pleased about the gift too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {来|き}てよかったです。ご{家族|かぞく}にもよろしくお{伝|つた}えください。
lines.romaji: Kite yokatta desu. Gokazoku ni mo yoroshiku otsutae kudasai.
lines.meaning: I'm glad I came. Please give my regards to your family too.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {天気|てんき}{予報|よほう}では、{夜|よる}は{雨|あめ}だそうです。{急|いそ}ぎましょう。

grammar.title: Modest language for your own side
grammar.formation: 言う → 申す; 行く/来る → 参る; する → いたす; いる → おる. Asking/visiting a respected person: 伺う; viewing a respected person's material: 拝見する.
grammar.explanation: Use modest forms for yourself or your own side. 申す・参る・いたす・おる can make speech formal to the listener without implying that every action is directed towards them. 伺う and 拝見する lower your action in relation to a respected person or their material. Do not call a visitor's action humble on their behalf. おります is common formal 'am/is here'; unit 7's いらっしゃいます raises the other actor.
grammar.example: 実習に参りました。
grammar.translation: I've come for the internship training (modest).

examples.ja: バオと{申|もう}します。
examples.en: My name is Bao (modest).

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}を{拝見|はいけん}します。
examples.en: I'll look at the materials (humble).

examples.ja: {会議室|かいぎしつ}におります。
examples.en: I'm in the meeting room (modest).

grammar.mistake: Use your own name + と申します. 先生がおります lowers the teacher rather than respecting them; use 先生はいらっしゃいます when respect is intended.

grammar.title: Put a question inside a sentence; name something
grammar.formation: Question word + plain clause + か + main verb. Yes/no plain clause + かどうか. Noun + という + noun. Before embedded か, noun/な-adjective present affirmative normally omits だ.
grammar.explanation: どの会議室を使うか確認します means checking which meeting room is used. There is one main statement, not two independent questions. 会議があるかどうか asks whether there is a meeting. ～という introduces a name or label: 青葉システムという会社. These constructions do not confirm the embedded proposition; someone can check whether a meeting exists without saying it does.
grammar.example: どの会議室を使うか確認します。
grammar.translation: I'll check which meeting room we will use.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}が{誰|だれ}か{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: I'll check who is in charge.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}があるかどうか{聞|き}きます。
examples.en: I'll ask whether there is a meeting.

examples.ja: {青葉|あおば}システムという{会社|かいしゃ}です。
examples.en: It is a company called Aoba Systems (fictional course company).

grammar.mistake: An embedded question does not need a question mark after か. Use 誰か here, not 誰だか in the formal pattern practised in this unit. という labels a name, not an ability or permission.

grammar.title: Easy to do, hard to do, without doing
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + やすい / にくい, conjugated as い-adjectives. Verb negative ない-form + で + following action.
grammar.explanation: 読みやすい describes something as easy to read; 使いにくい describes difficulty of use. These forms concern ease rather than your permission to do the action. ～ないで describes doing an action without another: 教科書を見ないで答えます. Distinguish this from ～なくてもいい, which removes an obligation, and from ～ないでください, a request not to do something.
grammar.example: 名前を確認しないで、電話をかけないでください。
grammar.translation: Please don't make the call without checking the name.

examples.ja: この{資料|しりょう}は{読|よ}みやすいです。
examples.en: These materials are easy to read.

examples.ja: この{電話|でんわ}は{使|つか}いにくいです。
examples.en: This phone is difficult to use.

examples.ja: {教科書|きょうかしょ}を{見|み}ないで、{答|こた}えます。
examples.en: I'll answer without looking at the textbook.

grammar.mistake: Use 読みやすい, not 読むやすい. ～ないで is not ～なくてもいい: 'without doing' and 'needn't do' describe different things.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Jisshū no Bao desu. Shiryō no tantō ga donata ka, kakunin shitai desu.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {森|もり}です。{私|わたし}に{聞|き}いてください。
lines.romaji: Mori desu. Watashi ni kiite kudasai.
lines.meaning: It's Mori. Please ask me.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {先|さき}ほど、{十時|じゅうじ}に{会議室|かいぎしつ}Aとおっしゃいましたね。{鍵|かぎ}は{受付|うけつけ}で{受|う}け{取|と}りますか。

lines.speaker: Mori

lines.meaning: Understood. I'll check the name, then enter the room.

exercises.context: You are describing your own arrival for training to a senior office colleague. Use modest language for your action.
exercises.prompt: Which is the requested modest introduction?
options: {実習|じっしゅう}にいらっしゃいました。
{実習|じっしゅう}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりました。
{実習|じっしゅう}に{参|まい}りました。

options: {資料|しりょう}の{担当|たんとう}を{確認|かくにん}したいです。
{夕食|ゆうしょく}をごちそうさまでした。
{鍵|かぎ}を{落|お}としてしまいました。

exercises.line: この{資料|しりょう}をご{覧|らん}ください。

options: {私|わたし}がご{覧|らん}になります。
{私|わたし}がおっしゃいます。
exercises.explain: 拝見します lowers your viewing action; ご覧になる raises someone else's viewing.

exercises.meaning: I'll check who is in charge.
